body.statement: For every finite \(X\), fixed \(\ell\), finite \(\mathcal I\ni\varnothing\), and loopless graph pair \(G,H\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G)\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H)\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\). Consequently, \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G)=\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H)\) if and only if both \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\) and \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(H,G)\) hold. This criterion is exact on lower-dimensional rank, cancellation, nullification, invisible-source, and source-symmetry strata, and it is a finite graph-generated compatibility representation rather than the original structural-existence formula.
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: a sound-and-complete equality criterion for joint response-kernel model sets under one shared mechanism and source tuple.
body.gap: Dai et al. characterize an observational zero-allowed class, and Zhou et al. characterize acyclic graphical invariances; neither covers exact-support cyclic parametric response-kernel law sets with shared source laws.
body.consumer: Perturbational feedback analyses such as Bicycle can report every hidden-variable graph compatible with all fitted population perturbation kernels instead of treating one graph as uniquely identified.
